correctness.rationale: The six published facet orbits reconstruct exactly 156 facets and the published face vector. Every one of 533 tetrahedral links is explicitly rebuilt and checked to be a cycle; the resulting length spectrum is exhaustive. The 91 short tetrahedra are partitioned by the 39-element affine action, and the 13-block orbit is checked pair-by-pair to have lambda one. For every index 1 through 5, every possible center face is exhaustively tested against the exact boundary-of-simplex link criterion and no move is found. The embedded verifier replays these checks from the published orbit representatives without external packages.

value.rationale: Short links are mathematically motivated in the primary literature as the local configurations enabling tight handle attachment. Classifying every such tetrahedron reveals an unexpected finite-projective-plane layer: one symmetry orbit is exactly a projective plane of order 3. The simultaneous absence of every positive-index bistellar move shows that these locally minimal links do not provide a simplicial simplification route. This is a structural statement about a canonical small triangulation, not an arbitrary slice or a face-count recomputation.
